summary: Marion Rastelli works in Indology and religious studies. She completed her doctoral studies under Gerhard Oberhammer and has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and the University of Vienna as a lecturer (attested 2020–2026).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and history, Mark A. Nathan earned his PhD from UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held positions at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman (~1990–1994), he worked at SOAS (~1994–1998) and became an Associate Professor at the University of Sydney.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2006) before joining the University of California, Berkeley, as Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures in ~2006.

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Bradford and earned his PhD from the University of Exeter (1988–1990). He lectured at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and became Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University (~2003).
Mark Hale works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts at Harvard University (attested 1987) and Concordia University (attested 1997).

Mark I. Wallace works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur (~1982–1986) and held posts at Georgia State University (~1987–1989) and Swarthmore College (~1989).

Mark Jan Dresden studied Iranian and Central Asian linguistics at the universities of Amsterdam and Utrecht, training under Jan Gonda, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Bruno Henning. He taught Iranian languages at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).

Mark Juergensmeyer studied at Columbia and earned a PhD from UC Berkeley (~1969–1974). A religious studies and Indology scholar, he has held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College.

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held posts at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2004–2006), and later served as Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).
Mark McClish is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies under Patrick Olivelle. He held a post at Birmingham-Southern College (attested 2012).
Mark Owen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Pedersen is a computational linguistics scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Queensland in 2001 and held an academic post there.

Mark Rowe is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He has held a faculty post at McMaster University, serving as Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2015, 2026).

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski studied Indology at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Oxford, completing his PhD (~1975–1979) under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson alongside study with traditional teachers.

Mark Siderits is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held appointments as Professor of Philosophy at Illinois State University (~1979–2008) and Seoul National University (~2008–2012).

Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge and studied under Elizabeth De Michelis. He has served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

Mark T. Unno works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College and Stanford University, holding academic positions at Brown University and the University of Oregon (~2000).

Mark Tatz specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, completing a PhD at the University of British Columbia (1978) under Leon Hurvitz while also studying under traditional teachers. He later served as Professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 1988).
